overall_reason: A near-black Linear-violet (#5e6ad2) dev-tool page with // mono kickers, a fake live metrics panel, a placeholder logo wall, three equal feature cards, a Sarah Chen testimonial, three pricing tiers and a CTA band: eight stock sections in stock order, so the specific copy sits on a default skeleton.

findings.where: whole page, section order at 1440 (tiles 1440-00 to 1440-03)
findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: nav, mock-dashboard hero ("skittie:live — metrics"), logo strip, stat band (18.4% / 9m / 2.1%), three equal feature cards, testimonial, three pricing tiers with a featured middle, CTA band ("Stop guessing. Start knowing."), link footer: 8 stock sections in stock order.
findings.before: Hero > metric panel > logos > 3 cards > quote > 3 tiers > CTA band
findings.after: Lead with one real artefact of the product (an actual funnel question typed in English and its answer) and cut the sections that repeat the template: logo strip, equal cards, CTA band
findings.why: Seven or more stock sections reads as generated regardless of copy quality; this is the default dev-tool landing order.

findings.evidence: "We found the exact step where users churned in a fifteen-minute session. Skittie paid for itself in one afternoon." — Sarah Chen, founder of Stitchboard. Sarah Chen is the canonical default-cast testimonial name; the sweep's default_names did not fire.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: a real customer quote with permission, name and company] or remove the section
findings.why: An invented quote from an invented founder is fabricated proof.

findings.evidence: "Trusted by 4,000+ indie teams" next to text-and-glyph pseudo-logos "acme", "fathom", "baseline", "radar", "promptly" (acme is the placeholder company). Sweep caught the 4,000+ count; the invented logo wall itself was not flagged.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real customer names with permission] or delete the strip
findings.why: Invented customer names presented as social proof.

findings.evidence: A styled-div dashboard titled "skittie:live — metrics" with a green "● live" dot showing trial_to_paid 18.4%, time_to_value 9m, churn_90d 2.1%, "median, n=4,120": a fake live product UI with fake data standing in for a screenshot.
findings.before: Hand-built metrics card with invented numbers and a live dot
findings.after: A real screenshot or recording of a Skittie funnel, or [DATA NEEDED: product capture]
findings.why: A dashboard mock with fake data is a look-family tell the sweep cannot see; the "live" dot claims a state that is not live.

findings.where: hero kicker, feature cards, CTA band
findings.evidence: Mono code-comment labels used as eyebrows: "// Product analytics for indie founders", "▸ funnels.realtime", "▸ replay.sessions", "▸ cohorts.smart", "// no credit card · no data team"; footer colophon "v2.4.1 — set in Space Grotesk & JetBrains Mono".
findings.after: Fold the category into the sub-line and drop the // and ▸ code dressing from non-code labels
findings.why: Code-comment eyebrows are the dark-single-accent family's signature (mono_labels tell, 17 instances); they decorate rather than inform.

findings.where: h1, final CTA h2, feature head
findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER lines that fit any analytics site: "Know exactly what your users do." (h1), "Stop guessing. Start knowing." (CTA h2), "Simple pricing". T-RIVAL-NAME: swap in PostHog or Mixpanel and all three stay true.
findings.before: Know exactly what your users do.
findings.after: A head only Skittie can say, built from its one real difference ("typed in English", "zero schema"), e.g. "Ask your product a question in English. Get the funnel."
findings.why: Hero and closing heads are the rival-swap-proof stock pair; the specific idea is buried in the sub-line.

findings.evidence: Three equal-width cards, same padding, same 1px border, same ▸ mono id + h3 + 14px paragraph recipe; T-DELETION: removing the ▸ mono ids loses nothing.
findings.after: Show one feature large with real output (a replay frame, a funnel) and list the other two as text
findings.why: Equal card triplets are the stock feature section; the card_kit detector missed it because there is no icon tile.

strengths: Some copy is specific and should survive: "Funnels that read like questions, not config screens", "No per-seat theater, no hidden events line", "Slice by ... typed in English".
Pricing tiers are concrete (events per month, retention days) rather than vague feature words.
not_investigated: No 00-contract.md: no brief override recorded for the dark-single-accent look, so it is treated as unchosen.
Buttons render in Liberation Sans fallback (form controls not inheriting Space Grotesk); already in sweep type_ladder, not repeated.
